milestone: DiDQube Phase 4 item 1 (execution plan §Phase 4): Factor is the first real consumer of the canonical resolveDiDQube resolver, migrating its own independent identity walk in the Use Case Zero readiness projection's agentShell leg.
problem: services/factor/useCaseZeroReadinessProjection.ts's resolveAgentShellLeg treated a bare agent_root_identity row (found via findAgentRootIdentityBySlug) as sufficient proof of 'agent shell established' -- it never checked whether that anchor was actually bound into its DiDQube constitutional container (the Phase 1 supertype tables: didqubes/agent_didqubes). This is exactly the class of gap Phase 4 exists to close: a consumer reasoning about identity via a raw anchor table lookup, parallel to (and unaware of) the canonical resolver Phase 2 built for precisely this question.
observedFailure: Code inspection: resolveAgentShellLeg's 'rootIdentity found' branch (useCaseZeroReadinessProjection.ts, prior to this change) returned state:'established' from findAgentRootIdentityBySlug's result alone, with no call to resolveDiDQube anywhere in the file.

Live query against the 'Aigent Z' Supabase project (bsjhfvctmduxhohtllly) confirmed the DiDQube Phase 1 tables (didqubes/human_didqubes/agent_didqubes) exist and, as of this session, all 19 existing agent_root_identity rows already have an agent_didqubes binding (0 unbound) -- so there is no LIVE data gap today, but nothing in the code protected against one emerging: any future agent_root_identity row created through a path that does not call the new ensureAgentDiDQubeBinding would silently pass agentShell as 'established' while remaining permanently unresolvable through the canonical resolver, invisible to every other Phase 4 consumer that will come to rely on it.

tests/activity-receipts-action-type-parity.test.ts failed immediately after adding the new 'agent_didqube_container_bound' action type to ActivityActionType, confirming the drift-incident regression guard (2026-07-24) still catches an unpaired TS-union/CHECK-constraint addition -- required a wholesale-rebuild migration before the addition was safe to ship.
rootCauses: Phase 2 (the resolver itself) and Phase 1 (the supertype tables) were built and verified in isolation, deliberately not wired into any consumer yet (the resolver's own module doc: 'NO consumer ... calls this yet'). Factor's readiness projection predates the resolver's existence and was never revisited once it shipped.

No mechanism existed to CREATE a DiDQube binding for an agent_root_identity row outside the one-time Phase 0 backfill script -- meaning even a consumer that wanted to check resolveDiDQube had no path to remediate an unresolved result short of a manual database operation.
resolution: services/identity/didQubeResolver.ts: added ensureAgentDiDQubeBinding -- a narrow, idempotent write path (the resolver's own module doc updated to name it as the ONE exception to 'writes nothing'). Never manufactures the agent_root_identity anchor; requires it to already exist. Handles the insert-race case by re-reading rather than assuming failure.

services/factor/useCaseZeroReadinessProjection.ts: added a new, distinct, REQUIRED leg 'didqubeContainer' (never overloading agentShell's own state) that calls resolveDiDQube against the resolved agent_root_identity_id and reports established/missing/blocked/unreadable honestly, mirroring the file's own established leg-state discipline. REGISTRABLE_AGENTS platform runtime agents (a separate identity model, out of scope for this pass) are reported established+optional so they never block.

services/factor/useCaseZeroOrchestrator.ts: added the 'didqubeContainer' actionable step, calling ensureAgentDiDQubeBinding ONLY when the leg's own state is 'missing' (never when 'blocked'/'unreadable' -- mirrors agentShell's own pre-mutation state check), writing a new LOCAL (non-anchored) 'agent_didqube_container_bound' receipt on success.

services/receipts/activityReceiptService.ts + a new migration (20260930300000_didqube_container_bound_receipt_action_type.sql, applied live) add 'agent_didqube_container_bound' to both the TS union and the activity_receipts_action_type_check CHECK constraint -- verified live via pg_get_constraintdef after apply.

tests/use-case-zero-orchestrator.test.ts: added a new describe block (5 tests) proving prepare-gating end-to-end through the REAL (unmocked) projection: an unresolved container is treated as a Factor-owned action and attempts to bind (one step per call, never chaining into case creation in the same call); ensureAgentDiDQubeBinding itself failing blocks rather than being treated as bound; a conflicted resolver state blocks without ever attempting to bind; a REGISTRABLE_AGENTS platform agent never invokes resolveDiDQube at all. Also updated the one pre-existing test this change affected to assert the new integration explicitly (resolveDiDQube called with the correct anchor id) rather than merely not regressing.
rejectedApproaches: Overloading agentShell's own existing leg state to also carry the DiDQube-container fact (e.g. treating a bound-but-not-DiDQube-resolved anchor as agentShell:'missing') -- rejected: this file's own architecture gives every distinct fact its own leg with its own orchestrator handler; conflating two facts into one leg's state would require the orchestrator to parse reason-string content to disambiguate 'no RootDID yet, genesis needed' from 'RootDID exists, container binding needed' -- fragile, and inconsistent with every other leg in this file.

Creating the DiDQube binding inside sponsorPolityAgent.ts's own genesis transaction (the shared, capacity/authority-gated agent-genesis primitive many other subsystems call) -- rejected as out of scope for a Factor-only vertical migration: touching a shared, heavily-documented primitive used across the platform is a larger, cross-cutting change the operator's 'do not perform another estate-wide audit between consumers' instruction argues against; the new didqubeContainer leg + orchestrator step achieves the same effect scoped entirely within Factor's own files, and is itself the reusable primitive (ensureAgentDiDQubeBinding) any future genesis-time caller can adopt later without another audit.

Adding 'agent_didqube_container_bound' to services/dvn/activityReceiptDvnPipeline.ts's ANCHORABLE_ACTION_TYPES -- explicitly NOT done. The operator's instruction keeps the DiDQube DVN consumer/payload migration behind its own required standalone approval (execution plan Phase 4 item 6); this receipt stays local-only.
unresolvedRisks: The 'bring your own agent' path grants Factor the ability to bind a DiDQube container for ANY existing agent_root_identity row it discovers by slug, not only ones it itself minted. Today this is safe (every existing row is already bound), but the underlying policy question -- who is authorized to complete a container binding for an identity they did not create -- was not separately ruled on; flagged rather than decided here, since it is the same shape of question the T0/T1 wallet-authority brief already resolved for Passport possession (prepare-gating is not authority), and no live data currently exercises the edge case.

No systematic canary yet enforces 'every consumer that reads agent identity must go through resolveDiDQube' across the codebase -- this migration covers Factor's own agentShell path only, per the operator's explicit 'do not perform another estate-wide audit between consumers' instruction. Aegis, CTP, DCIR, Standing, and Registry/Horizen remain unmigrated, tracked as their own separate vertical commits.
